formats.key: PermitWitnessTransferFrom(TokenPermissions permitted,address spender,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline,V2DutchOrder witness)DutchOutput(address token,uint256 startAmount,uint256 endAmount,address recipient)OrderInfo(address reactor,address swapper,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline,address additionalValidationContract,bytes additionalValidationData)TokenPermissions(address token,uint256 amount)V2DutchOrder(OrderInfo info,address cosigner,address baseInputToken,uint256 baseInputStartAmount,uint256 baseInputEndAmount,DutchOutput[] baseOutputs)
effects: The signer lets the spender (the UniswapX V2 Dutch reactor) pull the input token once through Permit2, up to permitted.amount, before the deadline.

The input that leaves the signer goes to the filler. It decays from baseInputStartAmount (the cosigner can only lower it) toward baseInputEndAmount. The reactor builds the Permit2 cap from baseInputEndAmount, so that is the real maximum.
Each listed recipient receives an output token from the filler, at least endAmount of it. The zero address means native ETH. Outputs to other addresses are fees that come out of the swap's value.
The cosigner sets the decay window and the exclusive filler. It can raise outputs or lower the input, but never go past the signed bounds.
The Permit2 nonce is used up, so the signature works only once.
formats.shown: The intent "UniswapX V2 Dutch Order", the raw spender, the approve amount, a 'Spend max' set to baseInputStartAmount, a 'Min amount to receive' and a raw 'On Address' for each output, and the approval expiry.

findings.title: V2DutchOrder 'Spend max' shows baseInputStartAmount, but the input can rise to baseInputEndAmount
findings.evidence: Descriptor field {"path": "witness.baseInputStartAmount", "label": "Spend max"}. In UniswapX DutchDecayLib.decay(DutchInput), the result is InputToken(input.token, decayedInput, input.endAmount): the input decays toward endAmount, and maxAmount = endAmount. V2DutchOrderReactor._transferInputTokens passes order.toPermit() with amount = input.maxAmount. On an exact-output order (start < end), the signer spends more than 'Spend max'. The real cap is shown only as 'Approve amount' (permitted.amount). This falls under not-critical #2, so it is a warning.
findings.fix: Remove the 'Spend max' field, or point it at witness.baseInputEndAmount with tokenPath witness.baseInputToken. Relabel permitted.amount as 'Max to spend'.

findings.title: V2DutchOrder labels every output 'Min amount to receive', including fee outputs paid to third parties
findings.evidence: Descriptor witness.baseOutputs.[] field {"path": "endAmount", "label": "Min amount to receive"}. Cases 0 and 1 show '5 USDC' as 'Min amount to receive' with 'On Address 0x3fC9…'. That is a fee output to another address, not something the signer receives.
findings.fix: Change the label to 'Min output' and the recipient label to 'Paid to', so that each output reads as a payment to the address shown.

findings.title: V2DutchOrder intent names the order type, not the swap and its tokens
findings.evidence: Descriptor "intent": "UniswapX V2 Dutch Order". A non-expert cannot tell from it that USDC leaves and WETH or ETH arrives (cases 0, 1).
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Swap with UniswapX" and add an interpolatedIntent naming the input amount and the min output.

findings.title: V2DutchOrder shows the spender and the output recipients as raw addresses
findings.evidence: Descriptor {"path": "spender", "label": "Approve to spender", "format": "raw"} and {"path": "recipient", "label": "On Address", "format": "raw"}. Cases 0 and 1 render 0x6000da47… and 0xd8dA6BF2… as plain hex, so the signer cannot see that the second address is their own.
findings.fix: Use format addressName, with types ["contract"] for spender and types ["eoa","wallet"] with sources ["local","ens"] for recipient.

findings.title: V2DutchOrder hides the cosigner, who sets the decay window and the exclusive filler
findings.evidence: Descriptor {"path": "witness.cosigner", "visible": "never"}. In V2DutchOrderReactor._updateWithCosignerAmounts, the cosigner can only lower the input below baseInputStartAmount and raise outputs above startAmount. It also sets decayStartTime, decayEndTime and exclusiveFiller. The shown endAmount floors still hold.

findings.title: V2DutchOrder hides additionalValidationContract and its data inside witness.info
findings.evidence: Descriptor {"path": "witness.info", "visible": "never"}. In the reactor, additionalValidationContract.validate(filler, order) only decides who may fill. It moves none of the signer's assets.

findings.title: V2DutchOrder test messages could not verify on chain and do not cover an exact-output order
findings.evidence: Case 0 has permitted.amount 2500000000 but baseInputEndAmount 2450000000, and deadline 1776988800 but witness.info.deadline 1776902400. Case 1 also has a top-level nonce 842119337502 against an info.nonce of 842119337501. The reactor builds the permit from info.deadline, info.nonce and input.endAmount, so these signatures fail. No case has baseInputStartAmount < baseInputEndAmount, the path where 'Spend max' is wrong.
findings.fix: Make the permit fields match the witness (amount = baseInputEndAmount, deadline = info.deadline, nonce = info.nonce). Add an exact-output case with a rising input.

couldNotCheck: Neither the Permit2 source (0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3) nor the UniswapX V2 Dutch reactor source (0x6000da47483062A0D734Ba3dc7576Ce6A0B645C4) is in the directory; contracts/COLLECT-FAILED.txt shows the Sourcify fetch failed. The input cap, the output decay and the cosigner rules were judged from public UniswapX code that is not here.
